To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a regularization to enforce the consistency of the encoder of a variational auto-encoder (VAE); (2) our method improves the quality of representations learned by a VAE, especially for downstream classification tasks, but also leads to improved generalization; (3) our method outperforms the triplet loss on 3D data, and can even outperform it on MNIST and CIFAR-10

(1) we propose a simple, general, and effective regularization method for VAEs, (2) this method consistently improves the quality of VAE-based learned representations, and (3) it also improves generalization of VAEs.

(a) the encoder of VAEs is not consistent; (b) this inconsistency can be regularized using the proposed regularization method that improves the quality of learned representations; (c) this regularization method is applicable to any type of VAE, and (d) when applied to NVAE, it yields state-of-the art performance on MNIST and CIFAR-10 and outperforms the triplet loss on 3D shapes
